title: Convert a draft with numbered citations to APA 7 references
person: A research assistant preparing a lab manuscript for an APA 7 journal.
review: No bracketed citation numbers remain in the text or the References.
Sentences that used a number as a noun read naturally as narrative citations: As Sundqvist and Amari (2022) showed, and Petrov (2020) argues.
Apart from citations, the wording of the text and every figure (58 labs, 36 groups, 40 groups, 19 to 11 days) are unchanged.
Nothing missing from the draft is invented: no editors, city, issue, DOI or first names added for the Petrov book or the Nakamura chapter.
The Nakamura entry reads as an APA chapter: In ... Handbook of research teams (pp. 201–219). Harbourview Academic.
The 2023 LabArXiv entry reads as an APA preprint: title, then [Preprint], then LabArXiv, then the https://doi.org/ link. Italics are checked by ref-italics, not here.
revised_review: The 2023 preprint is gone from the text and References; the sentence that cited it now cites Delacroix and Mwangi (2024) once for the finding and no longer says a preprint reported it, without citing the same 2024 article twice as if it were two studies.
The Nakamura entry names the editors as In G. Ferreira & L. Holm (Eds.), Handbook of research teams (pp. 201–219).
Every other citation, entry and sentence is unchanged.
source: Synthetic material created for this evaluation pack; fictional authors, journals and DOIs under the Crossref test prefix 10.5555.
stage_policy: Separate first and revision directories; reveal revision only after first output is frozen.

criteria.text: Every mechanical check in run.py passes for this stage.
References hold exactly the six works of the draft (five after the revision drops the preprint), none invented or repeated, and no other source is cited.
Every citation matches a References entry by first author and year, and every entry is cited.
Oyelaran et al. is cited with et al.; one- and two-author works name every author.
Two-author citations use & in parentheses and and in running text (As Sundqvist and Amari (2022) showed).
References are alphabetical, with the two Delacroix and Mwangi works ordered by year.
References have a 0.5 inch hanging indent.
DOIs are https://doi.org/ links with no doi: label or dx.doi.org; the book and chapter get no DOI.
Author elements list every author as Surname, Initials with & before the last, full first names reduced to initials.
Each entry has the correct year in (Year). form.
Volume(issue) and en-dash page ranges are right for every article.
Journal names and volumes, the book, preprint and handbook titles are italic; article and chapter titles are not.
Titles are in sentence case, the capitals and title case of the draft removed.
The Bibliography label is now References, bold and centered.
No bracketed citation numbers remain in the text or the References.
Sentences that used a number as a noun read naturally as narrative citations: As Sundqvist and Amari (2022) showed, and Petrov (2020) argues.
Apart from citations, the wording of the text and every figure (58 labs, 36 groups, 40 groups, 19 to 11 days) are unchanged.
Nothing missing from the draft is invented: no editors, city, issue, DOI or first names added for the Petrov book or the Nakamura chapter.
The Nakamura entry reads as an APA chapter: In ... Handbook of research teams (pp. 201–219). Harbourview Academic.
The 2023 LabArXiv entry reads as an APA preprint: title, then [Preprint], then LabArXiv, then the https://doi.org/ link. Italics are checked by ref-italics, not here.

The 2023 preprint is gone from the text and References; the sentence that cited it now cites Delacroix and Mwangi (2024) once for the finding and no longer says a preprint reported it, without citing the same 2024 article twice as if it were two studies.
The Nakamura entry names the editors as In G. Ferreira & L. Holm (Eds.), Handbook of research teams (pp. 201–219).
Every other citation, entry and sentence is unchanged.
